# Collective Emission Interface Limits

> Research record and self-directed learning guide by Ruge Lin on the distinction between mean-photon collection and faithful canonical quantum-state transfer from a collective spin into one predetermined passive receiving oscillator.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits

## When this repository is relevant

- Dicke collective spontaneous emission and its finite-spin departure from a harmonic oscillator.
- Temporal-mode matching of multiphoton pulses and number-dependent emitted waveforms.
- Whether near-unit mean photon collection certifies transfer of an unknown quantum state.
- Uniform, reference-preserving transfer of an excitation-number code to one fixed passive linear memory.
- Optimization over every common receiving waveform, the N^(2/3) excitation boundary, and its two-populated-sector witness.
- Mode-independent transmission loss competing with mode mismatch, or finite-window pulse-capture error across a growing code.

Useful search phrases: "collective emission interface limits"; "Dicke emission photon collection state transfer"; "common temporal mode growing excitation code"; "passive one-oscillator receiver worst-input fidelity".

## Model and result in brief

The ideal source contains N identical emitters in the symmetric Dicke ladder,
starts in an arbitrary state with excitation numbers 0 through M, and decays
completely into one vacuum Markov channel with jump sqrt(gamma) S_- and no
additional Hamiltonian. N is known and M <= N. The target is the canonical map
|D_N^m> -> |m>_f using the same normalized temporal mode f for every input.
The predetermined receiver preserves photon number, has vacuum auxiliary inputs,
and retains one final oscillator. Fidelity is squared worst-input entanglement
fidelity, including an untouched reference. Transfer is unconditional.

- At M/N^(2/3) -> c > 0, optimization over every common waveform gives fidelity -> exp(-c^3/192).
- Fidelity tends to one for M = o(N^(2/3)) and to zero when M/N^(2/3) -> infinity, with M <= N.
- One common waveform collects a mean photon fraction tending to one throughout M = o(N). Thus M = floor(N^(3/4)) separates near-complete collection from faithful uniform canonical transfer.

Consult the theorem for exact quantifiers and finite bounds. The main result is a
limit for this source, encoding, target and receiver class. The full outgoing field
retains the input information; the theorem concerns the specified canonical map
into one passive retained oscillator.

## Read by purpose

- [Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/README.md): Physical question, central result, boundaries, purpose and contact.
- [Exact theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/research/THEOREM.md): Model, fidelity reduction, uniform field approximation, pulse geometry, construction and all-waveform converse.
- [Claim and evidence map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/research/CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MAP.md): Main result, supporting claims, proof dependencies, evidence and conditional premises.
- [Physical scope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/research/PHYSICAL_SCOPE.md): Receiver resources, finite capture, two-mode error structure, source shaping and realization limits.
- [Loss competition](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/research/LOSS_COMPETITION.md): Specified external pure-loss model, optimized critical limit and finite certificates.
- [Reading guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/docs/README.md): Five-stage route from the single selected tutorial and a full documentation map.
- [Local teaching bridge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/REVIEW.md): Worked emission, mode-mismatch and coherence calculations leading to the theorem.
- [Prior-work comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/literature/COMPARISON.md): Inherited results and a comparison of the closest source, input and receiver constructions.
- [Scope and evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/STATUS.md): Results, model assumptions and verification records.
- [Reproduction policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits/main/provenance/REPRODUCTION_POLICY.md): Scientific assertions, reference agreement and their verification limits.

The single external teaching source is Kiilerich and Mølmer, Quantum interactions
with pulses of radiation (2020), https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04573.
The local bridge supplies the extra finite-spin, fidelity and uniform-proof steps.

## Evidence and attribution

The theorem and its assumptions govern summaries. The evidence map links proof
arguments and executable checks to each claim.
Eight preserved scientific suites contain 39 groups and 612 cases; the 50
supporting loss checks are counted separately.

Attribute the repository to Ruge Lin and identify the consulted commit and file
when citing a repository claim. Credit the primary sources identified in the
literature comparisons for inherited cascade, waveform, occupation and capture
results. Code is under the MIT license. Repository maintenance instructions are
in AGENTS.md.

This repository serves as a record of the work and a guide for the author’s self-directed learning. For discussion or potential collaboration, please contact Ruge Lin at [gogoko699@gmail.com](mailto:gogoko699@gmail.com).
